evidence.observation: The patch removes the child from the registry as soon as both pipes reach EOF, then waits without the registry. The deadline can only stop children still in the registry.

findings.verification: Run the bounded runner against a fixture process that closes both pipes and waits, then assert that its PID is gone when the deadline returns.
findings.remedy: Keep the direct child under deadline ownership until exit is confirmed, including when both pipes close first.

findings.claim: Two writers can both pass the pre-rename checks. The loser treats every rename error as 'use .eck for this run' and does not re-check whether .c3 now exists and .eck is gone. write_answer then create_dir_all's that path, so a new .eck appears beside the moved .c3. Doctor reports both folders and merges nothing, leaving the loser's report and journal stranded.
findings.trigger: Two c3 finish (or snapshot/manifest) processes start together on a repository whose only project folder is a real .eck/, using the default .collab directory so the move happens inside ensure.

evidence.observation: migrate_legacy checks that .c3 is absent, then rename; any Err becomes deferred and ensure sets dir to legacy_path and returns.
write_answer calls create_dir_all on Ensured.dir before writing last-report.md.
Layout::Both prints a warning that both folders exist and tells the operator to merge by hand.

findings.verification: RC1.
findings.remedy: After a failed rename, stat again. If .c3 is a real directory, use it. If .eck is absent, return an error. Never create_dir_all the legacy path unless it is still the original directory.

findings.claim: The post-rename relocation of the old tool's anchor, update_seq, telemetry_queue.json and lastsnapshot/AnswerToSA.md runs only inside the same migrate_legacy call as the successful rename. The next run sees .c3 and returns, so those files stay at the top of .c3. The cache move then refuses to replace an existing .c3/anchor, and read_anchor treats the old tool's file as C3's snapshot baseline.
findings.trigger: The process is killed after .eck has been renamed to .c3 and before the leftover renames finish, or a leftover rename fails because the file is busy. A later c3 snapshot or c3 finish --snapshot runs.

evidence.observation: If symlink_metadata(.c3) succeeds, migrate_legacy returns an empty Migration before the leftover loop.
Leftover and report renames happen only after the folder rename in that same function.
An existing destination name is left in place. read_anchor returns any non-empty .c3/anchor text.

findings.verification: RC2.
findings.remedy: Make the leftover relocation idempotent: whenever .c3 is a real directory, move those four names into legacy/ or last-report.md if the destination is absent, before migrate_collab_cache.

findings.claim: Link refusal covers the .eck directory entry that would be renamed, and misses three writes. ensure treats a symlink .c3 as the project folder because is_dir follows it, then writes stubs through it. The report step renames lastsnapshot/AnswerToSA.md through an intermediate symlink and can move a file that lives outside the folder. migrate_collab_cache renames cache entries out of a collab directory reached by walking a symlink .eck, so the link target loses those files.
findings.trigger: .c3 is a symlink to a directory, or .eck/lastsnapshot is a symlink to an outside directory containing AnswerToSA.md before the first move, or .eck is a symlink to a tree that contains collab/.c3 and the command's collab root is .eck/collab.

evidence.observation: symlink_metadata Ok followed by dir.is_dir() accepts a symlink-to-directory; stubs are then std::fs::write'd under that path.
The report path is .c3/lastsnapshot/AnswerToSA.md. symlink_metadata on the file follows the intermediate directory link, and rename moves that file when is_file is true.
The .eck link itself is not renamed. migrate_collab_cache still renames children of collab_root/.c3, and that path follows an intermediate .eck symlink.

findings.verification: RC3.
findings.remedy: Require a real directory (symlink_metadata, is_dir, and not is_link) for both .c3 and every parent used in a rename. Refuse the report move when any component of lastsnapshot is a link. Skip cache migration when any ancestor of the source is a link.

findings.claim: Resolving a collab path inside .c3 while a real .eck still exists calls migrate_legacy from collab_dir. c3 pack, c3 explain (including when --out is set, and before the write confirmation), and c3 index query all resolve the collab root on their read path, so a command that should only read can rename the project folder.
findings.trigger: The repository has a real .eck/ and no .c3, and the operator runs c3 pack, c3 explain --out, or c3 index query with --collab-dir .c3/collab.

evidence.observation: For a .c3 path, when .c3 is absent and .eck is a directory, collab_dir calls migrate_legacy unless the hook flag or C3_CHILD is set.
resolve_collab_root runs before the pack is built and before the y/N confirmation; --out still takes that path.
The index reader and pack both call resolve_collab_root, which calls collab_dir, before any read-only work.

findings.verification: RC4.
findings.remedy: Move the folder only from ensure and from c3 doctor --fix. collab_dir on a read path should return the legacy path, or the mapped path, without calling migrate_legacy.

findings.claim: Collab spelling is decided on the path string before canonicalize. A relative path whose first component is not .c3 or .eck, because a .. segment comes first, is returned unchanged. After the folder has moved, a writer that create_dir_all's that path creates a new .eck/ and stores the new consultation there while the moved records stay under .c3/.
findings.trigger: After .eck has been renamed to .c3, run c3 consult --detach --collab-dir sub/../.eck/collab --task t (or .c3/../.eck/collab).

evidence.observation: split_state_path uses repo_relative text and the first non-dot component. sub/../.eck/collab classifies as outside the state folder.
collab_dir runs first. canonicalize is only applied afterward, and a missing path is returned unchanged.
Detached consult joins the resolved collab root with the task and create_dir_all's it before starting the run.

findings.verification: RC5.
findings.remedy: Canonicalize, reject .., and require the result to stay under the repo before split_state_path. If the canonical path is under .c3 or .eck, map it. If the legacy path is missing, do not create it.

findings.claim: The guard that should stop a move while a detached consultation or work run is live under .eck fails open and is not held until the rename. An unreadable directory, a run_dirs error, or a pid whose start time cannot be read counts as not live. A run that starts after the check and before rename is moved with the folder.
findings.trigger: A detached consult or work run is live under .eck/collab/<task>, its status directory cannot be listed or its owner start time cannot be read, or it is started in the gap after live_run_under returns and before rename.

evidence.observation: walk uses read_dir(d).ok()?; a listing error returns None, which live_run_under treats as nothing live.
run_dirs Err is skipped by if let Ok, so those runs are invisible. task_is_live then returns false.
process_start_iso None makes pid_alive false. The live check returns before rename with no lock held across the two calls.

findings.verification: On Linux, start a detached run under .eck/collab/t whose pid start time is unreadable to this user, then run c3 finish and see whether .eck was renamed. Separately, start the run in the window after the check.
findings.remedy: Treat an unreadable directory or run record as live. Hold an exclusive lock on the folder from the check through the rename, and have detached consult and work take the same lock before creating their task directory.

findings.claim: With C3_STATE_MIGRATE=off or state_migrate false, the rename is skipped, and a collab path under .eck is returned unchanged. A detached consult then creates its task directory under .eck, so the switch does not keep every write off that folder.
findings.trigger: C3_STATE_MIGRATE=off, the repository still has .eck/collab, and the operator runs c3 consult --detach --collab-dir .eck/collab.

evidence.observation: migration_enabled false returns before rename and collab_dir returns the given path.
The README says the switch means C3 never touches .eck/ and creates a fresh .c3/.
create_dir_all on the resolved task directory writes under the given .eck/collab path.

findings.verification: With C3_STATE_MIGRATE=off, run a detached consult with --collab-dir .eck/collab and compare .eck/collab before and after.
findings.remedy: Document that the switch stops the rename only, or refuse a collab path inside .eck while the switch is off and require an explicit directory outside it.

findings.claim: Reviewer packs, snapshots, and c3 fetch drop a directory named .c3 or .eck at any depth. A --diff patch excludes those names only as root pathspecs, so a nested .c3/ or .eck/ directory is still written into the patch that is handed to the reviewer.
findings.trigger: c3 consult --diff HEAD while a tracked or untracked nested directory such as pkg/.eck/ contains a file the ignore rules do not exclude.

evidence.observation: diff_excludes adds root pathspecs for STATE_DIR and LEGACY_STATE_DIR only.
is_hard_ignored_dir calls is_state_component on every directory name the walk sees.

findings.verification: Add a tracked file pkg/.eck/secret.txt, run c3 consult --diff on a range that contains it, and inspect the patch bytes.
findings.remedy: Exclude any path component equal to .c3 or .eck under the same names_equal rule the pack walk uses, including nested paths.

findings.claim: CI split does not survive cancellation: with `if: success() || failure()` a cancelled (timed-out/hung) crate step skips the remaining crate steps, so the exact hung-run scenario the split was built to diagnose still yields only the running step's log.
findings.trigger: A test step is cancelled (45/30 min timeout, manual cancel, hung runner) instead of failing.

evidence.observation: Check job uses one step per crate (c3-core, c3, c3-cli), each `if: success() || failure()`; same pattern in the index-surreal job. In GitHub Actions a cancelled step makes `failure()` false for later steps, so they are skipped; `always()` (or `!cancelled()`) would be needed. Workspace members are exactly these three crates (Cargo.toml), so coverage is otherwise unchanged and the c3 index-surreal feature exists (crates/c3/Cargo.toml), i.e. failures still run all steps — only cancel skips.

findings.verification: Cancel a run mid-test-step and confirm the later crate steps still execute and report.
findings.remedy: Use `if: always()` on the per-crate test steps (job outcome still reflects the failure/cancel).

findings.claim: Address table misses three IPv4-embedding IPv6 forms: Teredo 2001::/32, 6to4 2002::/16, and deprecated IPv4-compatible ::/96 (plus ISATAP). `to_ipv4_mapped` unwraps only ::ffff:0:0/96 and the code unwraps only the NAT64 /96 prefix; the other forms pass `is_public_address` as global even when the embedded IPv4 is private/loopback.
findings.trigger: A name lookup or redirect hop answering a Teredo/6to4/compat address whose embedded IPv4 is non-global.

evidence.observation: NON_GLOBAL_V6 lists unspecified, loopback, 64:ff9b:1::/48, 100::/64, 2001:db8::/32, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, fec0::/10, ff00::/8 — no 2001::/32, no 2002::/16, no ::/96 compat range. is_public_address unwraps mapped and 64:ff9b::/96 only. Lookup-side (any-bad refuses) and peer-side checks plus the pinned-resolver are otherwise complete.

findings.verification: Unit-test is_public_address against 2001:0:<priv>:… , 2002:0a00:1:: and ::10.0.0.1; confirm currently returned as public.
findings.remedy: Add 2001::/32 and 2002::/16 to the table (or unwrap their embedded IPv4 like NAT64) and refuse ::/96 compat addresses; add one row per range to the address tests.

findings.claim: The whole-entry fingerprint makes benign concurrent edits fatal to a good update: any added annotation key, inert ext field, or semantically-null JSON respelling between the gate snapshot and the smoke changes the SHA-256, so the smoke reports 'not run' and a passing engine update is rolled back / a swap abandoned.
findings.trigger: Operator (or another session) edits the seated entry in any field while its pre/post smoke is in flight.

evidence.observation: bound_roster refuses when entry_fingerprint(text) != fingerprint, where the fingerprint is SHA-256 of the canonical whole entry object; the swap flow binds fingerprint from the pre-smoke basis and smokes against it. Fail-closed by design, but the blast radius includes edits that change nothing the smoke executes.

findings.verification: Edit an inert field of the seat between the two engine-update smokes in the e2e harness and observe rollback of a passing update.
findings.remedy: Keep fail-closed, but document that any roster edit during a pass holds that entry's update; optionally scope the fingerprint to executed fields (endpoint, auth, plan, key var, model, protection flags).

findings.claim: A roster with no file path can never be smoked: fingerprint_now returns '' and bound_roster refuses an empty fingerprint unconditionally, so every engine update for such a roster is held on every pass with only a per-smoke line, instead of one loud refusal.
findings.trigger: Maintain runs against a roster with empty `path` (tests, embedded use).

evidence.observation: fingerprint_now returns String::new when roster.path is empty; bound_roster errors when fingerprint.is_empty(). pick_target still returns a seat, so the pass proceeds to a smoke that cannot run.

findings.verification: Call pick_target on a file-less roster and run_smoke; confirm perpetual 'not run' Fail rather than a single clear refusal.
findings.remedy: Return None from pick_target (or abort the engine step loudly) when the fingerprint is empty for a file-backed expectation.

findings.claim: An explicit 'no fixed price' marker bypasses the cross-major price hold: list_price keeps only positive finite numbers, so OpenRouter's "-1" (router, no fixed price) and "0" become 'no price', and price_hold returns None — the swap proceeds with no announcement, in the direction (unknown cost) the hold exists to catch.
findings.trigger: Catalog prices the seated id but marks the higher-major candidate '-1' (or vice versa).

evidence.observation: list_price drops '-1'/'0'/non-numeric (positive-finite filter); price_hold fires only when a source prices BOTH ids and the ratio exceeds 2. Documented intent covers 'without prices for both ids', but '-1' is affirmative unknown-price, not missing data.

findings.verification: Feed parse_catalog a candidate with pricing {prompt:'-1'} and confirm price_hold is None and the swap proceeds.
findings.remedy: Treat an explicit '-1' on either side as unknown-price and hold/announce the cross-major swap (keep '0'/free seating).

findings.claim: is_public_address accepts IPv6 addresses that embed a non-global IPv4, and the IPv6 benchmarking range, so a public-catalog lookup and every hop's peer check allow them. Deprecated IPv4-compatible ::10.0.0.1 (::a00:1), 6to4 2002:a00:1:: (embeds 10.0.0.1), Teredo 2001::/32, and benchmarking 2001:2::/48 are outside NON_GLOBAL_V6 and are not unwrapped. Only ::ffff:0:0/96 and 64:ff9b::/96 are unwrapped.
findings.trigger: A maintain catalog or page name resolves to one of those addresses, or the connected peer is one of them.

evidence.observation: NON_GLOBAL_V6 lists ::/128, ::1/128, 64:ff9b:1::/48, 100::/64, 2001:db8::/32, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, fec0::/10, and ff00::/8. is_public_address unwraps to_ipv4_mapped and 64:ff9b::/96 only, then tests the two tables.
resolve_within refuses the name only when some address fails is_public_address, and fetch's peer check uses the same function.
2002:a00:1:: embeds 10.0.0.1 and ::a00:1 is the deprecated IPv4-compatible form of 10.0.0.1. Both miss the tables, so is_public_address returns true.

findings.verification: In crates/c3, assert is_public_address is false for ::a00:1, 2002:a00:1::, a 2001::/32 Teredo address, and 2001:2::1, beside the_address_classes_of_a_public_source.
findings.remedy: Unwrap 6to4 (2002::/16) and IPv4-compatible (::/96) to the embedded IPv4 and judge that address. Deny 2001::/32 and 2001:2::/48 outright.

findings.claim: When the candidate's vendor has no seated row, price_hold divides the candidate's list price by the first same-name row in that catalog. A decoy row with a high price makes a much more expensive successor look within 2x, and swap mode seats it.
findings.trigger: One public source lists, in order, decoy/qwen3.8-max at prompt 100, qwen/qwen3.8-max at prompt 0.000001, and new/qwen4-max at prompt 0.01, and the roster seat is qwen3.8-max in swap mode.

evidence.observation: seated_entry prefers the candidate vendor, then hits.first().
list_price_ratio uses that pair per field and keeps the max finite ratio. price_hold returns None unless the max is greater than 2, and run_models seats when price_hold is None.

findings.verification: Add the three-id SourceList above to a_successor_across_a_major_priced_over_twice_the_seated_one_is_announced_only and expect a price_hold. Today the first-row ratio is 0.0001, so the candidate is seated.
findings.remedy: Pair prices only when the seated id is under the candidate's vendor. If no same-vendor seated price exists, leave the ratio unset for that hit.

findings.claim: A seated list price of 0, a negative price, or a price present on only one of prompt and completion produces no ratio, so a higher-major successor of a free or one-sided seat is seated.
findings.trigger: Catalog pricing.prompt is "0" or "-1" for the seated id and a positive number for a higher-major successor, or the two ids are priced on different fields.

evidence.observation: list_price keeps a field only when it is finite and greater than 0. "0" and "-1" are dropped.
A field is compared only when both ids have it. With no pair, list_price_ratio returns None and price_hold does not hold the swap.

findings.verification: Unit-test seated prompt "0" and candidate prompt 0.01 across a major. Expect price_hold to be None and the candidate to remain seatable.
findings.remedy: Treat a known zero seated price as cheaper than any positive candidate price across a major, and hold. Keep ignoring a missing price.

history.note: As F38-5: decided in the wave's brief and said in the CHANGELOG - the list price is a signal; without a positive price for both ids on the same field nothing is held.

findings.claim: catalog_alias accepts a leading token that matches the endpoint host's lab even when that token is neither the rest's maker nor the plan slug. The successor is written with that token put back.
findings.trigger: Roster model kimi-qwen3.8-max, plan alibaba, endpoint host under moonshot.ai, catalog id qwen/qwen3.8-max with a successor qwen/qwen4-max.

evidence.observation: The alias is refused only when token_lab differs from model_lab(rest), lab_named_by(plan), and host_lab. host_lab is lab_of_host, which returns moonshot for moonshot.ai and kimi.ai.
aliased_view prefixes every id of the matched vendor with the roster token, so the written successor is kimi-qwen4-max.

findings.verification: Call catalog_alias on that entry with a source containing qwen/qwen3.8-max and qwen/qwen4-max. Expect Some(prefix kimi-) and swap candidate kimi-qwen4-max.
findings.remedy: Allow the host lab only when the plan slug is empty. Require token_lab to equal the rest's maker or the plan slug.

findings.claim: The codex smoke requires switch evidence on every turn in the rollout file, including turns that are not this smoke's consults. A resumed thread whose older turn has no in-boundary multi_agent_version or tool list is unproven, and the engine update is held or rolled back.
findings.trigger: Two smoke consults resume one codex thread whose file already contains a completed turn with no turn_context multi_agent_version and no additional_tools between its task_started and task_complete.

evidence.observation: After boundary_errors and the completed count, the check returns unproven at the first TurnEvidence with evidence false, over the whole turns vector.
Evidence is recorded only on the open turn. A turn_context or tool list outside task_started..task_complete does not mark a turn. The reader comment states a rollout keeps the thread's history.

findings.verification: Extend the_codex_smoke_proves_the_switch_for_each_turn_of_a_shared_rollout with an older completed turn that has no in-boundary evidence, then two evidenced smoke turns. Expect Unproven.
findings.remedy: Require evidence only on the last k turns, where k is the number of smoke consults on that thread, and still reject unpaired boundaries inside that suffix.

history.note: The codex smoke always starts its own thread (first consult new, second resumes it), so the rollout holds only the smoke's turns; requiring evidence on every turn of that file is the stricter reading of F32-2.

findings.claim: Outside test mode the in-use hook is ignored. With CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE on and CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MAINTAIN_IN_USE unset, engine_in_use returns false for every engine, so a real maintain pass updates a CLI that is running.
findings.trigger: A production c3 maintain --run process with CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1 and the hook unset, while grok or codex is running.

evidence.observation: engine_in_use returns in_use_by_hook immediately when mode_on() is true and does not read the process table.
in_use_by_hook treats a missing hook as no engine in use. mode_on is true only for 1, true, yes, or on.

findings.verification: With CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE=1 and the hook unset, call engine_in_use for grok while that process exists. Expect false. With the mode unset and the hook set to grok, expect the process table to decide.
findings.remedy: Keep the hook test-only. In test mode, if the hook is unset, keep the fail-closed in-use result for any engine the test did not name, or refuse maintain updates while test mode is on.

history.note: Test mode is test mode: with CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_MODE on, the in-use probe is answered by the test hook by design (the debt it closes: tests read the real process table).
